title: GRID_ALPHA=46 cites an 18% "map.odin" grid blend; the game canon is 9% and lives in view.odin
evidence: tools/render_dublin_preview.py:33: `GRID_ALPHA = 46       # 18% of 255 — map.odin grid blend`; docstring: "-> park -> grid (18% blend) -> streets -> spawn candidates -> district"; line 102: "# --- grid (18% blend over land AND water — map.odin) ---". app/render/view.odin:528-534: "// v2-look-polish evening pass (LEFOU): the grid was the second-loudest / // element on the frame (\"reads as graph paper\") — the MM whitespace cut / // halves the 7.1 blend again (18% → 9%): the snap lattice stays visible / // for placement, but the paper reads clean under the ribbons. / g, c := p.grid, p.canvas / grid_soft := rl.Color{ / u8((u16(g.r)*9 + u16(c.r)*91) / 100),"
detail: The game blends grid at 9% into canvas (9/91) since the LEFOU evening pass, in view.odin map_draw — not map.odin. Previews render the snap lattice ~2× stronger than current canon, and misattribute the source.
recommended_fix: Set GRID_ALPHA ≈ 23 (9% of 255) or replicate the 9/91 grid-into-canvas mix; update the comment and docstring to 9% and view.odin map_draw.

title: Preview claims canon draw order but renders land as palette.canvas; map.odin canon is palette.land
evidence: tools/render_dublin_preview.py:91: `img = Image.new("RGBA", (W, H), hex_to_rgba(palette, "canvas"))`; docstring: "Draw order mirrors map.odin canon: land -> water -> coast". app/render/map.odin:257: `return p.land // Land + any defensive fallback = the warm land tint`. app/render/view.odin: "The landmass renders the warm land tint (map.odin map_color → palette.land), distinct from the paper canvas." data/palette.json: land -> [239, 228, 186, 255], canvas -> [237, 226, 200, 255].
detail: The tool claims to use the game's OWN tokens and mirror canon, but never uses palette.land; game Land cells render the warm land tint, distinct from the paper canvas. The user-gated previews (and the recipe a follow-up copies) show paper-colored land.
recommended_fix: Fill the board area with palette.land before water/coast/park (keep canvas for letterbox margins), or correct the docstring to drop the canon-mirroring claim.

title: osm_extract.py imports io and shapely's shape() but never uses either
evidence: tools/osm_extract.py:49: `import io`; :59: `from shapely.geometry import LineString, Point, Polygon, shape`. grep for `io.` returns 0 matches; `shape` appears only in the import line and comments/docstrings ("user-approved shape", "same pipeline shape", "keep their shape").
detail: Two unused imports — orphan code; `shape` in particular suggests a removed code path (relations were meant to use shapely.shape at some point).
recommended_fix: Delete `import io` and drop `shape` from the shapely.geometry import list.

title: `if args.bake or True:` — the --bake flag is dead, the bake path always runs
evidence: tools/osm_extract.py:586-590: `if args.bake or True:` / `fetch_raw(args.cache)  # cache-first: no network when present` / `bake(cache_dir...)` style block — the condition is always True, so argparse's `--bake` (`ap.add_argument("--bake", action="store_true", help="bake dublin.json from cache (fetch if missing)")`) never changes behavior.
detail: Always-true conditional makes the documented --bake flag inert and misleading: bare invocation and --bake take the identical path (fetch + bake + verify).
recommended_fix: Remove `or True` and make bare invocation (no flags) the fetch+bake+verify default, or drop the --bake flag from argparse and the docstring.

title: New third-party deps (shapely, pyproj, certifi, Pillow) are undeclared — no requirements manifest exists
evidence: tools/osm_extract.py:59-60: `from shapely.geometry import LineString, Point, Polygon, shape` / `import pyproj`; :380-383: `import certifi / ctx.load_verify_locations(certifi.where())`; tools/render_dublin_preview.py:25: `from PIL import Image, ImageDraw, ImageFont`. No requirements*.txt/pyproject.toml/Pipfile exists in the repo; Dockerfile.ci installs only `ca-certificates curl git build-essential clang python3 \`.
detail: PIL has host-only precedent (blur_gate.py), but shapely/pyproj/certifi are new with no manifest; a fresh checkout can't run the bake without undocumented manual installs.
recommended_fix: Add tools/requirements.txt (shapely, pyproj, certifi, Pillow) or list install commands in the tools' docstrings/README.

title: render_dublin_preview.py re-implements osm_extract.py's board-fit math instead of importing it
evidence: tools/render_dublin_preview.py:181-190: `# Tile coords for crop anchors (same math as osm_extract.bake).` / `import pyproj` / `tr = pyproj.Transformer.from_crs("WGS84", "EPSG:32629", always_xy=True)` ... `ox0 = cxm - (b["w_tiles"] / scale) / 2.0` / `utm_top = cym + (b["h_tiles"] / scale) / 2.0`. tools/osm_extract.py:354-368: `ul = transformer.transform(BBOX_W, BBOX_N)` ... `ox0 = cxm - (BOARD_W_TILES / scale) / 2.0` ... `utm_top = cym + (BOARD_H_TILES / scale) / 2.0`.
detail: The UTM fit/letterbox math exists twice; if osm_extract's fit changes, crop anchors silently drift. osm_extract.py is importable (has __main__ guard) and already exposes the constants.
recommended_fix: Import osm_extract from render_dublin_preview.py and reuse its transformer/constants (or factor the fit into one shared helper both tools call).
